changes.after: Raise signals an exception. A matching rescue can handle it and show its message.

before: raise ArgumentError, message stops the normal path by raising an exception. A begin/rescue region handles matching classes; rescue ArgumentError => error binds the exception object, whose message explains the failure.

An unqualified rescue handles StandardError subclasses, not every Exception. Rescue only failures you can meaningfully handle; catching too broadly can disguise programming mistakes. Code after the failing expression in begin is skipped.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
begin
  minutes = -1
  raise ArgumentError, "positive minutes required" if minutes <= 0
  puts minutes
rescue ArgumentError => error
  puts error.message
end

```
Expected output or behavior: positive minutes required. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why rescuing Exception is broader than rescuing StandardError. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
begin
  minutes = -1
  raise ArgumentError, "positive minutes required" if minutes <= 0
  puts minutes
rescue ArgumentError => error
  puts error.message
end
```
The output is `positive minutes required`. Negative one fails the check, so the message prints instead of the number.
